title: Reading: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, Year 449
subtitle: Her Martianus and Valentinus onfēngon rīce...
objectives: Understand and apply the concepts of Reading: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, Year 449.
Read and parse examples from authentic Old English texts.

sections.heading: Core concept
sections.body:
Her Martianus and Valentinus onfēngon rīce and rīcsodon seofon winter. And on hiera dagum Hengest and Horsa, fram Wyrtgeorne gelaþode, Bretta cyninge, gesōhton Bretene on þǣm stede þe is genemned Ypwinesfleot.

Translation: 'In this year Martianus and Valentinus received the kingdom and ruled seven years. And in their days Hengest and Horsa, invited by Vortigern, king of the Britons, sought Britain at the place which is called Ebbsfleet.'

This is the Chronicle's account of the arrival of the Anglo-Saxons in Britain. Legendary, not historical, but essential to the Anglo-Saxon origin story.

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: This passage marks the traditional date of the Anglo-Saxon settlement of Britain.

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.body: Her (here = in this year), onfēngon (received, past pl. of onfōn), rīce (kingdom, acc.), rīcsodon (ruled, past pl.), seofon (seven), winter (years, acc. pl.), hiera (their, gen. pl.), dagum (days, dat. pl.), gelaþode (invited, past part.), cyninge (king, dat. sg.), gesōhton (sought, past pl.), stede (place, dat. sg.), genemned (named, past part.).
